title: Settling into old age
caption: The galaxy NGC 3384, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3384 · constellation Leo · about 35 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, B. Lehmer et al.

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: NGC 3384 glows softly, rounded and largely featureless, much like a typical elliptical galaxy. Such galaxies seldom show signs of recent star formation and are dominated by old, ageing, reddish stars. That sets them apart from lively spirals like the Milky Way, which hold many young, blue stars in arms that swirl around a bright core.

NGC 3384 has a twist, though. Towards its centre it shows a hint of a disc, in the form of a bar of stars cutting across the middle. Many spiral galaxies have bars too, the Milky Way among them. Bars are thought to channel material through and around the core of a galaxy, helping to keep the activity there going.
The galaxy lies approximately 35 million light-years away in the constellation Leo, the Lion. The picture was taken with the Advanced Camera for Surveys on the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.27 x 3.38 arcminutes) and distance (35 million light years), the frame spans roughly 33,000 × 34,000 light-years. Its light set out about 35 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys observed NGC 3384 through g and z filters at 475 nm and 850 nm. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Hubble's exposures gather far more light than an eye can, which helps bring out the hint of a central bar.
